annotation.summary_en: Opinion of the German Ethics Council (March 2020) on robotics in care for older and disabled people. Using "good care" as the guiding concept, it analyses assistive, monitoring and companion robots at micro, meso and macro levels of responsibility. It recommends that robots complement rather than replace human care, along with high safety standards, adapted liability law, participation, and training for care staff.
key_provisions_or_claims: Robots must complement, not substitute, interpersonal care; only persons can be bearers of moral responsibility

High safety standards via strict rules on manufacture, approval and use, plus strict liability without exclusion, burden-of-proof rules and insurance; legislator should review medical device and liability law
Transparent responsibility structures to prevent erosion of responsibility; evidence of improved care quality before inclusion in standard coverage
Robot use must respect wellbeing, self-determination, identity, relationality, privacy, intimacy and shame; robots must not be used for deception or manipulation
Robot funding must not cut resources for care staff; care curricula and further training should cover new technologies and their ethics
